summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.17/894)

data.turoyo: D umarwo “Mdayənli ḥamšo (5) noṭat...“ mdayanwole, lə mawbalwo bir umarwo “1 b Nisən!“ umarwo “Hawən luxat!“ <...>
data.translation: The one who would say ‘Lend me five banknotes ...’, he would lend it to him; he would not take it back, but would say ‘The first of April!’ He would say ‘Let it be yours!’ <...>

rationale: First Infectum-wa box; -le is recipient after the habitual form, as the preceding loan request makes explicit.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.49/2184)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: E kətwolle ḥtiyaǧ. U ḥtiyaǧaṯṯe, d luwewolle ḥtiyaǧ qay gəd maydiwo? Hən mənayye saymiwo taǧara bənne, hən mənayye kətwolle ḥtiyaǧ, masala həwewolle sniquṯo laǧan hawxa šəqliwo. U ḥa d luwele sniyaq qay gəd gorəš? W hən mənayye ste masala, saymiwo šuġlone bənne, hən ste mayko kuḏaʕno... Walḥasəl mdayniwo.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: Well, they had a need. Their need: if they had not had a need, why would they take it? Some of them would trade with it, some of them had a need, for instance a need would arise for them, so they would take it like that. Someone who has no need, why would he draw it? And some of them, for instance, would do jobs with it; others, how should I know... In any case, they borrowed.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa/1 cell; the preceding need and taking-money clauses establish borrower-subject direction.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.49/2194)

data.translation: Uncle Isho: They would lend it to them, they would lend it to them as a loan for God's sake. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa/1 cell; repeated plural lender form with a cognate loan noun and recipient suffix; quote the repetition once.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 86/53)

data.turoyo: Zbaṭ məlle l oḏər, omər: "Ya oḏər." Omər: "Ha." Omər: "Dayalli tre yawmo d samno šeliye." Mdayallele tre yawme, səmle šeliye yaqurto, qafili aʕ ʕeze.
data.translation: Da sprach der Februar zum März: "März, borge mir zwei Tage, damit ich frieren lasse". Er borgte ihm zwei Tage, und jener liess es heftig frieren, so dass die Ziegen erfroren.

rationale: Dünne Preterit-Zelle: Geber statt bestehendem Kreditnehmer; Tage als verliehener Gegenstand.

data.translation: und sprach zu ihm: "Bruder, leihe mir fünf Groschen, ich gebe sie dir in dieser Woche zurück."

rationale: Eigener Geldleih-Imperativ: 86/5 steht fälschlich beim Monatsbeleg, dieser Vers hat tatsächlich Mdayanli.

data.translation: When I would go with the children to the library to borrow storybooks, we always had an obstacle.

data.turoyo: ʕAṭiya Xamri: Maṯlo i naqla dəwelan mfarǧono, uʕdo d kəmfarəǧ, kətle rənyo d koṯəw kṯowo ʕal mede, kəple mən šəkəl, yaʕni kəple oṯe l gabayxu, mdayən a kṯowe aw šoqəl a kṯowe, mən šəkəl koʕawditu?
data.translation: Atiya Xamri: For example, when we have a viewer who is watching now, who has the idea of writing a book about something, how can he, that is, can he come to you, borrow the books or take the books? How do you work?

rationale: Thin Infectum/1 cell; singular borrower and book object corroborate the library participant extension.

summary: Remove the extra d in k-middayən
rationale: The cited verse has W Balliṭa kmidayən w lo kobe mede, with one d. The base-form pair of this same block is mdayən/midayən, also with one d in the Infectum. The extra d in the example is not a clitic-boundary or accent difference.

summary: Zwei geerbte II-Sektionen bleiben getrennt sichtbar: mdayalle/mdayən mit gemischter Glosse; mdayən/midayən mit englischer Glosse to borrow (money). Ein neuer Stamm I wird nicht erzeugt.

Valenz: Mdayallele zeigt Geberagens, l-Empfänger und Tage-NP; 51/30 hat Kreditnehmeragens mit ʕal ḥasab als Kreditgrundlage. 86/3 kontrastiert kəmdayən und kmidayən, beide mit habituellem Vergangenheitsbezug ohne -wa.

The first inherited II section has a broad lend/borrow gloss; the second II section remains separately visible with its own forms and wording. Jan does not resolve their morphological relation, so no duplicate-entry correction or Detransitive relabelling is made.

mdayanwole has lender subject and recipient -le in a request-response sequence; mdayniwo with need and taking money has borrower subject. Context and arguments establish direction, not a general rule from the shared base.
dayno d Aloho supplies a cognate loan noun with a religious qualifier. Interest-free status is not explicit in this verse and is not added to the gloss.
Ist kmidayən synchron ein Detransitive zu mdayən oder selbständige II-Variante? Zweite Sektion nicht ohne morphologische Bestätigung umetikettieren.
51/30: aktives mdayalle mit Kreditnehmeragens gegenüber Geberagens in PrS 86/53; Polysemie oder anders abzugrenzende Konstruktion? Bestehende gemeinsame Glosse vorerst erhalten.
Does borrowing mdayniwo differ morphologically from lending mdayniwonne, or only in valency? Resolve with the round-1 mdayən/midayən question.
What precisely does dayno d Aloho denote in Jan 1.49/2194: a charitable loan, an interest-free loan, or a formula for lending for God’s sake?
Should the second II block be the detransitive subsection of the first?
rationale: The first II block gives mdayalle/mdayən and its notes include Detransitive. A second block labelled II instead gives mdayən/midayən and the borrowing use of 86/3. This form pair and the existing Detransitive marker suggest that the second block is the detransitive subsection, but the supplied representation alone does not establish whether the source heading or its extraction is wrong.
